paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. God says their loyalty is like a morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes (Hosea 6:4). Mist looks lovely, but it's gone before the day gets going. God isn't asking for a show. He wants a faithfulness that is still standing at noon.

That's why He says, "For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings" (Hosea 6:6). Gifts and rituals can look great while the heart stays far away. I think that's the hard part, because you can do all the right things and never once get to know Him. Even in the middle of all that heat, God says not one of them calls upon Him (Hosea 7:7).

So the question for you, baker, is whether your faithfulness shows up every morning or only when it's convenient. And look how God starts: "What shall I do with you?" (Hosea 6:4). That's how a Father talks when He is not done with His people. He promises Judah a harvest when He restores His people from captivity (Hosea 6:11). So call on Him today, and keep it up, because He's the One who heals and restores. The story isn't over!
